chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, who said:
I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say, 'One prayer in the Mosque of Kufah is equal to one thousand prayers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the Mosque of Kufah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the spiritual prestige of the Mosque of Kufah, a site deeply intertwined with the history of the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly Imam Ali’s (AS) caliphate and martyrdom. By equating one prayer there to a thousand elsewhere, it emphasizes the concept of *fadilah* (virtue) attached to specific sacred spaces, encouraging believers to seek out these locations for heightened devotion and connection to the Imams.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥasan ibn Sa’īd, from Żarīf ibn Nāsiḥ, from Khālid Al-Qalānisi, who said:
I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say, “Establishing one prayer in the Mosque of Kūfah is equal to establishing one thousand prayers (elsewhere).”
